body:
PR-2776 round 2, item 1 evidence. One PR is over 60 s. Your ruling is needed BEFORE I push.

METHOD. `pr ship --dry-run` returns before the mandate scan (pr_cmd.rs ~2942 vs ~3064), so I used option (b). A temporary, uncommitted harness calls mandate_ship_cover on real open PRs from the primary checkout. It skips only the mandate-state and grant checks and stops before decide(). Everything up to that point is real: forge reads, verdicts, trace collection, store snapshot, the history batch, and the ledger. The ledger was redirected to a scratch AIDA_HOME. Binaries are this PR's code, built with the agent profile (the one `aida dev build` ships) and with debug.

FINDING 1: the batched history walk was still the bottleneck. `git log --all -- <101 paths>` alone took ~53 s, because git checks every pathspec against every commit of the ~53k-commit store history. NEW COMMIT ef1204a48c walks `-- objects` once and filters the names in-process. The results are identical: the existing equivalence test against the per-spec walk passes, and a new assertion pins the single pathspec. Strictness is unchanged: --all, ACMRT, fail-closed. That walk now takes ~9 s whatever the spec count.

NUMBERS (scan to decide, agent profile, after the fix):
- #2776 (96 specs): 15.6 / 13.1 / 12.6 s, median 13.1 s, load 37-48.
- #2725 (402 specs): one attempt takes 24-31 s. Runs were 60 s (2 attempts), 106 s (3 attempts, then refused "store changed"), and 107 s (3 attempts), median 106 s, load 10-31.
- Debug build: #2776 was 309 / 59 / 127 s before the fix and 29.5 / 24.8 / 24.5 s after. #2757 (2 specs) was 22.6 s median.

FINDING 2 (the cause of the >60 s): store_snapshot is pre-existing on main (mandate_traces.rs:79). It compares `show-ref --head` over ALL 5,369 refs of the shared repo, because .aida-store is a worktree of the code repo. Any agent's code push or fetch invalidates the attempt, so a ~30 s attempt rarely survives. On main it refuses outright; this PR's retries only reduce that.

PROPOSED FIX: on a snapshot mismatch, treat the attempt as stable iff no changed or added ref brings any new objects/ version, i.e. `git log --all --not <old tips> -- objects` is empty and HEAD is unchanged. A deleted ref only removes versions, so the evidence already gathered stays a superset (stricter). That is exact and fail-closed, but it changes a mandate gate (STRICT tier).

ASK. Pick one:
(A) Push now as is: AC3 is met per attempt and for typical PRs; file the snapshot scoping as a follow-up bug.
(B) Add the snapshot fix to this PR as a round-2 addition.
(C) Something else.
I recommend (A): it keeps this PR in scope and puts the gate change under its own STRICT review. Meanwhile I'm merging origin/main and running the gates. I will push only after your answer.
subject: PR-2776 item 1: timing evidence + a >60 s finding; ruling needed before push
